thread:
lee_s: Customer escalation — customer on Dedicated reporting duplicate POST processing and double billing. They say their app sees a 401, SDK refreshes token and retries, and the backend accepted the upload twice. They attached logs and a billing spike.
lee_s: Environment: Node 20.6, undici 5.16.0, @redwood/sdk v1.5.3, Dedicated. They use an automatic token refresh middleware that swaps tokens async.
devon_k: Do we already check if request bodies are rewindable before retrying? I thought we buffered in some codepaths but maybe not for multipart/stream uploads.
maria_g: Streams from fs.createReadStream or streaming multipart (form-data) are not cloneable. undici will try to re-send but the stream is consumed. If app doesn't re-create stream on retry, you'll get duplicate processing if server accepted on first attempt.
ryan_h: Can customer provide a minimal repro? I suspect a Readable stream + 401 on first attempt triggers our retry path.
devon_k: I whipped up a tiny repro to confirm (paste):
```js
// repro-stream-retry.js
import fs from 'fs'
import { request } from 'undici'

async function send(filePath, url) {
  const stream = fs.createReadStream(filePath)
  // simulate SDK behavior: send, on 401 refresh token and retry same request object
  const r1 = await request(url, { method: 'POST', body: stream, headers: { 'x-payload-id': 'payload-xyz' } })
  // if 401 -> refresh token and retry using the same body reference
}

// running this against a simple test server with a forced 401 on first call reproduces double POST
```
devon_k: On my test server I see two POST requests with the same payload-id within ~1-2s.
maria_g: Short-term mitigation: ask customers to send an Idempotency-Key header or to buffer the upload before passing to the SDK (read file into Buffer for small files). Also update docs: "Non-rewindable request bodies (node streams, some multipart) may result in duplicate downstream side-effects if retried. Use Idempotency-Key or buffer the body."
ryan_h: Long-term options:
- Buffer small request bodies automatically in SDK before retry (configurable threshold)
- Detect non-cloneable bodies and fail-fast with a clear error advising idempotency or buffering
- Add SDK opt-in to disable automatic retry-on-401 for non-GET non-idempotent methods
lee_s: Customer asks for ETA; can we prioritize a short patch that prevents silent retries on non-rewindable bodies and surfaces a clear error and remediation steps?
maria_g: I'll prototype a guard in the TS SDK: before retry, run isStream(body) && !isCloneable(body) -> throw new Error('SdkRetryError: non-rewindable-body - retries disabled for non-cloneable request bodies. Use Idempotency-Key or provide buffered body.'). We'll log details and include a link to support KB.
devon_k: I'll add unit tests: mock a Readable that cannot be recreated and assert SDK does not re-send and throws our SdkRetryError. Also add an integration test against a small server that returns 401 once.
ryan_h: I'll take the runtime side if it's just detection + message. Can we also surface a Console toggle for Dedicated accounts: "Enforce idempotency for writes" so ops can block double-charges while we ship an SDK fix?
lee_s: Filed INF-1437: "TS SDK: detect non-rewindable request bodies before retry to avoid duplicate POSTs / billing" and attached redacted logs from customer. https://redwood.example/infra/INF-1437
ci-bot: Created canary build for TS SDK v1.5.4-rc.2 including non-rewindable-body detection. Please smoke test.
lee_s: Customer accepted the suggested workaround (Idempotency-Key) for now and asked for billing remediation; I've looped in finance and account owner. ETA to customer: "short patch next week".
maria_g: Suggested customer snippet we can add to KB:
```js
// small-file workaround: buffer before upload
import fs from 'fs'
import { v4 as uuid } from 'uuid'
const buf = await fs.promises.readFile('./small.jpg')
await client.post('/upload', { body: buf, headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': uuid() } })
```
devon_k: Also documenting common pitfalls: streaming multipart via form-data libraries may hide that underlying transport is non-rewindable. Add troubleshooting steps for support to ask: "Are you passing a Node Readable stream or Buffer?"
ryan_h: Follow-ups: add telemetry to detect when we would have retried a non-cloneable body and surface in Console per-route warnings so customers can proactively fix.
lee_s: Thanks all. I'll update the customer thread with the workaround and the ticket link. Assigning INF-1437 to maria_g for prototype and devon_k for tests. :pray:
ci-bot: deploy-bot: canary build 1.5.4-rc.2 created for testing.
